learning_outcomes.text: Students are introduced to procedures and methods for identification, design, analysis of dynamical models of mechanical systems.

syllabus_topics: Theoretical basis concerning the vibrations of single- and multi-degree-of-freedom mechanical systems
Identification of structural and modal system parameters
Practical examples concerning the application of techniques
Identification of the structure of a machine tool
Simulation of dynamical response of a machine tool
Effect of localized structural modifications on a machine tool
Diagnostic application: identification and localization of a damage (crack) in an operating rotating shaft
Free and forced vibration of single and multi-degree-of-freedom systems, real and complex damping
Experimental modal analysis (EMA): time and frequency domain identification techniques
Application examples: machine tool model identification and structural modification
Application examples: crack identification and localization
teaching_methods: Lectures with blackboard and slides and notebook+overhead projector
Learning by doing (numerical and experimental activities concerning modeling and measuring of real mechanical systems)

assessment_methods.method: Oral examination (discussion of topics listed in the program, discussion of a specific topic or solution of a numerical application concerning mechanical vibrations)
